patch_description: Structural redesign from a monolithic sliding-window filter into a modular streaming pipeline with pluggable stages. Data flows through: (1) an adaptive Kalman smoothing stage whose noise covariance adapts to innovation magnitude, (2) a slope estimator using local polynomial regression on the Kalman state, (3) a hysteresis-based trend classifier that suppresses false reversals, and (4) a zero-lag blend that phase-corrects the smoothed estimate back toward the raw signal. Each stage is an independent class implementing a common `process(sample) -> state` interface, wired by a `Pipeline` orchestrator, enabling easy substitution (e.g., swap Kalman for particle filter). This improves maintainability, testability, and lets each optimization objective be isolated and tuned independently, while the phase-compensation stage explicitly targets lag error rather than treating it implicitly.
